key_idea: The remaining candidates always form an interval [l,r] and the cost of a bid depends on its absolute value, so do minimax interval DP over the bid x.
sketch: d[l][r] = min over x in [l,r] of max(x + d[l][x-1], b + d[x+1][r]), where the first term (overbid or exact hit, you pay x and continue below) is at least x and the second exists only if x<r. Bidding outside the interval never helps. O(n^3) = 6.4e7/6 operations for n=400, trivially fast; answers fit in int. Pitfall: unlike classic guess-the-number, cost is asymmetric (pay the bid when too high, pay b when too low) so no binary-search shortcut.
